correctness.rationale: The cut trace over the seven opposite prime-field labels gives an indicator of the kernel of the transposed cross matrix; the normalized reduced state has one eigenvalue p^{-r} per coset, yielding r log_2(p) for the positive-order Rényi and von Neumann entropies. A cut with k point vertices X has k line vertices Y on its opposite side; its cross matrix has the two complementary incidence blocks N[X,Y] and N[X^c,Y^c]^T. Exactly one seven-set of each complementary pair contains the distinguished point. An independent exact computation of determinantal divisors reproduced all eleven Smith classes across these 1,716 cuts, and modular elimination verified the geometry and reported field-rank counts. The Smith census contains only 2 and 3 as nonunit prime divisors; 28 cuts with factors (1,1,1,1,1,1,6) and one with (1,1,1,1,2,2,6) lose one unit mod 3. Hence the counts ranked 4 through 7 are (21,273,729,693) at 3 and (21,273,700,722) for every prime at least 5. Independently, using a noncollinear triple as a basis of F_2^3, its side lines yield a J-I block of order three; the complementary block can be ordered as I_3 bordered by ones and bottom-right zero, of determinant -3. The characteristic-three rank of this latter block is three. For the canonical point–line cut NN^T=2I+J gives determinant magnitude 24 and rank six mod 3, using the all-ones kernel and rank six of the product. Each of the 28 triangle sides has four points, uniquely identifying the triangle and the representative with four points. The independent exhaustive comparison excludes further defects. The p>=3 restriction pertains to the stated classification; it is not necessary for the character-orthogonality rank identity itself, which also holds at p=2. No extension to different graphs, weights, or composite dimensions is asserted.

value.rationale: Balanced cuts of the canonical Fano incidence graph are a natural setting for checking how entanglement depends on the prime field. The census determines the exact law for all odd primes and reveals that the visible point–line rank defect is not isolated: the other losses are exactly the noncollinear-triple cuts. The explicit witnesses and exact frequencies can be used as finite benchmarks and go beyond the standard computation for the full incidence matrix, without implying a general theorem for all planes.
